title: Advisory On Phishing Scams Involving Singpass
summary: Scammers sent Singpass-like SMSes threatening account deactivation and linking to spoofed login pages that requested Singpass credentials and OTPs.

title: Police Advisory On Phishing Scams Involving Fake Buyers On Online Marketplaces
summary: Fake marketplace buyers used purported order or delivery messages and links to redirect sellers to spoofed bank or delivery websites that collected personal information, banking credentials, card details, and OTPs.

title: Advisory On Technical Support Scams
summary: Fraudulent browser alerts led victims to scammers impersonating software-support personnel who instructed them to download remote-access applications and approve bank transactions using digital authentication tokens.

title: Police Advisory On Cryptocurrency Scams Involving Malicious Links And Unauthorised Transactions
summary: Scammers used messages and fraudulent websites to distribute malware through fake software updates and to solicit cryptocurrency payments or wallet connections through impersonated ticketing, token, and streaming services.

title: Police Advisory On Investment Scams
summary: Scammers used social and messaging platforms, posed as investment representatives, collected personal particulars, and directed victims to fraudulent platforms where they transferred money or cryptocurrency and later paid increasing fees while being unable to withdraw supposed profits.

title: Police Advisory On Job Scams
summary: Fake job offers delivered through messaging and social platforms directed victims to scam websites and required increasingly large transfers to bank accounts, PayNow numbers, or cryptocurrency wallets before supposed earnings could be withdrawn.

title: Police Advisory On Lucky Draw Scams Involving Facebook Live
summary: Facebook livestreams promoted scratch cards or lottery tickets, after which purported winners were asked to pay administrative fees through PayNow QR codes to claim cash prizes.

title: Police Advisory On Social Media Impersonation Scams Arising From Compromised Whatsapp Accounts
summary: Scammers obtained WhatsApp verification OTPs, took control of accounts, impersonated the account owners to their contacts, and requested emergency money transfers.

title: Joint Advisory On Safeguarding Against Compromise Of Cryptocurrency Assets
summary: Victims lost cryptocurrency after opening phishing links to spoofed wallet or exchange pages, and after keying in unfamiliar commands supplied by scammers, which authorised transfers out of their own wallets. Issued jointly by CSA and the Singapore Police Force.

title: Joint Advisory On Scams Involving Digital Manipulation
summary: Scammers used artificial intelligence to create or alter synthetic media, such as deepfake video and audio, to make fraudulent approaches appear credible. The advisory sets out precautions for businesses, and was issued jointly by CSA, the Singapore Police Force and the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

title: Alert On Scammers Impersonating CSA, The SPF And The MHA
summary: Scammers posing as officers from the Cyber Security Agency, the police and the Ministry of Home Affairs issued fake criminal investigation notices alleging involvement in a cyber-infiltration case, then pressured recipients to respond within 48 hours to avoid supposed criminal charges.

title: Job Scams
summary: Reference guidance on job scams, where victims are offered work-from-home tasks paid by commission, such as making advance purchases or boosting product listings and ratings, or are asked to move funds through their own accounts. Victims discover the scam when commissions never arrive or funds cannot be withdrawn.

title: E-Commerce Scams
summary: Reference guidance on e-commerce scams involving goods or services sold without a physical meet-up. Buyers pay and receive nothing, while sellers deliver and are shown forged payment screenshots. Warning signs include payment taken outside the platform, limited-time pricing, and links or third-party apps sent to arrange payment or refunds.

title: Joint Advisory On Uptick In Government Official Impersonation Scam Variant Featuring Impersonation Of Banks
summary: A government official impersonation variant that begins with an unsolicited call from someone posing as an officer of a local bank such as DBS, OCBC or UOB, asking the victim to verify transactions they did not make. Denial leads to a transfer to a purported government official. Issued jointly by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Singapore Police Force.

title: Joint Advisory On Impersonation Scams Involving Chinese Messaging And Payment Platforms
summary: Victims received unsolicited calls from local numbers placed by scammers posing as WeChat, UnionPay or Alipay staff, who claimed a subscription was about to renew and walked victims through supposed cancellation steps that led to losses. Issued jointly by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Singapore Police Force.
